purpose: Categorise AI evaluation instruments for comparing capabilities. Review unit: Chapter 6 within the volume.
intended_reviewers: AI evaluation researchers and instrument selectors; chapter describes student raters.
concepts_and_criteria: 18 facets under Validity, Consistency and Fairness. These groups address what is measured, how it is measured and which system is measured.
answer_format_and_guidance: Facet specific categorical values, explanations and examples. Some values express preferences; other facets categorise purposes without a universal preferred value.
missing_information: Reliability allows N/A when methodology or common use is unclear. This is not identical to an explicit finding of poor reliability or inapplicability.
accessibility_and_effort: Definitions and guided rating. Raters were AI related undergraduate/graduate students; time taken in hours was requested (printed p. 104). This records effort collection, but the chapter does not report a comparative novice accessibility or time saving result. Agreement is not correctness.
evaluation_and_findings: 36 instruments; first two rated by coordinators and all raters, next eleven by four raters, then two per instrument. Discussion led to revisions. Harder facets included Capability, Coverage, Specificity, Adjustability and Ambition.
evidence_assessment: Application and rater discussion provide evidence of use, not validation for general readers. Do not call the 18 facets a benchmark quality scale.
evidence_locator: Chapter 6, printed pp. 99–118, especially pp. 100–110; PDF pp. 101–112. Table 6.1 and facet definitions pp. 101–102.
